description: Detailed US Jet Age technology tree (1945-1960) across 7 branches: aero, structures, propulsion, avionics, armament, manufacturing, testing.

nodes.historical_note: NACA 6-series laminar-flow airfoils, Prandtl-Glauert compressibility correction, and WWII high-speed dive recovery flaps (P-80A, FH-1).
Robert T. Jones NACA TN-1033 (1945) & Operation Lusty German Busemann/Lippisch data enabling 35-deg swept wings (XP-86, XF-88).
Aerodynamically actuated leading-edge slats derived from Me 262 experience, taming swept-wing tip stall on the F-86A Sabre.
NACA 64A/65A-series transonic sections down to 9-10% t/c with straight trailing-edge slopes (Bell X-1 8%/10% wing, F-86 9.5% root).
Bell X-1 movable horizontal stabilizer discovery (1947) and F-86E 'flying tail' solving transonic shock-induced elevator lock.
Convair XF-92A (1948) and Douglas XF4D-1 Skyray pioneering low-aspect-ratio 60-deg delta and modified-delta planforms.
NACA boundary-layer diverters and cheek/wing-root splitter plates preventing fuselage boundary-layer ingestion.
45-deg quarter-chord sweep with 6-7% t/c airfoils for supersonic level flight (North American YF-100A, Vought XF8U-1).
Full-span leading-edge camber droop and Krueger flaps restoring CLmax on sharp-nosed thin supersonic wings.
Bell X-5 (1951) and Grumman XF10F-1 Jaguar translating-pivot variable-sweep mechanisms; heavy and mechanically complex in the 1950s.
Richard Whitcomb's NACA RM-L52H08 transonic area rule ('wasp waist'), cutting transonic wave drag by ~50-60% on YF-102A and F11F-1.
Ferri/NACA oblique-shock cone and half-cone inlets (Lockheed XF-104 fixed shock cones) for efficient pressure recovery above M1.4.
Biconvex 3.36% t/c low-aspect-ratio supersonic wings (Douglas X-3, Lockheed XF-104 Starfighter) minimizing supersonic wave drag.
Wing fences, sawtooth leading edges, vortex generators, and flush antenna fairings reducing interference/excrescence drag and shock-induced separation.
NACA conical camber leading edge for delta wings (production F-102A, F-106A, B-58), substantially cutting induced drag at high altitude.
Compressor-bleed boundary-layer control (BLC) blowing over trailing-edge flaps (F-104C/G, F4H-1 Phantom II) cutting approach speeds by 15-20 kt.
Multi-shock variable-angle external/internal compression ramps and translating cones with boundary-layer bleed (F-105, F-106, F-107A, F4H-1) for Mach 2+.
Jones/Whitcomb Mach-cone oblique-plane supersonic area rule optimizing cross-sectional distribution for Mach 1.5-2.2 cruise/dash (F-106A, F8U-3).
Alcoa 75S (7075-T6) high-strength aluminum alloy semi-monocoque construction and 8.0g USAAF fighter limit load standards.
Double-skinned torsion-box wing structure with tapered heavy aluminum plates (F-86 Sabre), resisting aeroelastic twist on swept wings.
BuAer jet carrier suitability standards: high-sink-rate oleo struts, hydraulic wing-fold joints, and keel-mounted arresting hooks (F2H, F9F).
Kroll-process commercially pure and early Ti-8Mn alloy sheets for aft-fuselage afterburner heat shields and frames (X-3, F-100A, F4D-1).
One-piece machined integrally stiffened wing skins eliminating thousands of rivets and sealing integral wing fuel tanks (F-100, F-104, A4D).
Adhesive-bonded aluminum and fiberglass honeycomb core sandwich panels for high stiffness-to-weight control surfaces and delta wings (F-102, B-58).
Fail-safe multi-load-path structural design and cyclic spectrum fatigue testing following early jet service crack discoveries.
Vacuum-melted Ti-6Al-4V alpha-beta alloy forgings and skins solving hydrogen embrittlement (F8U-1/2/3, F-101B, F4H-1).
PH 15-7Mo precipitation-hardening stainless steel brazed honeycomb and high-fraction titanium for sustained Mach 2.4-3.0 thermal structures (XF-108, YF-12/A-12).
Whittle/GE I-40 (Allison J33) double-sided centrifugal turbojet with Hastelloy-B/Vitallium hot section.
NACA 8-stage axial compressor cascade research & GE TG-180 (J35) / Westinghouse 19XB (J30/J34) single-spool axial turbojets.
S-816 cobalt-base and Inconel X/Nimonic 80A wrought nickel-chromium turbine buckets enabling J47 and J48 durability.
NACA Lewis tailpipe reheat flameholders and two-position clamshell eyelids (Solar/Westinghouse J34-WE-32 on XF6U-1, F-94A, F-89A).
12-stage fixed-geometry axial compressors with interstage bleed valves (GE J47-GE-13/27, Allison J35-A-29, Wright J65).
P&W Willgoos Turbine Lab and NACA Lewis Propulsion Systems Lab refrigerated high-altitude test cells preventing costly flight-test surprises.
Pratt & Whitney JT3 / J57 split-compressor (two-spool) architecture achieving OPR 11.5-12.5 without low-RPM compressor surge (Collier Trophy 1952).
Continuously variable iris/petal convergent-divergent nozzles and screech-damped flameholders (J57-P-7/P-21 on F-100/F-102).
Vacuum-induction-melted Waspaloy/M-252 turbine blades and titanium LP compressor rotors saving ~200 kg per J57 engine.
Gerhard Neumann's GE J79 17-stage single-spool compressor with variable stator vanes: high OPR (12-13.5) at far lower weight and frontal area than twin-spool.
NACA transonic compressor rotor blading enabling 24,500 lbf class high-airflow cores (Pratt & Whitney J75 / JT4A on F-105, F-106).
Internal convection air-cooled HP turbine vanes and blades (J58, J93, late J79), pushing TIT beyond uncooled alloy melting limits.
Front-fan / aft-fan turbofan architectures (P&W JT3D / TF33, GE CJ805-23, early TF30 studies) slashing subsonic cruise TSFC.
WWII SCR-522 VHF radio, Mk 18 / K-14 lead-computing gyro sight, cockpit pressurization, SCR-720 night-fighter AI radar, and AN/APG-5 gun-ranging radar.
3,000 psi irreversible hydraulic flight control actuators with artificial feel (F-86, F-84E, F-100), overcoming transonic hinge moments.
Ballistic catapult pilot ejection seat (tested on P-61B and FJ-1 in 1946); mandatory for high-speed jet bailout.
Sperry AN/APS-19 3-cm X-band radar allowing single-seat carrier night fighters (F4U-5N, F2H-2N).
Sperry A-1CM / A-4 analog computing sight coupled to GE AN/APG-30 automatic rangefinder radar (F-86A/E/F).
Rate-gyro yaw and pitch dampers (first flown on Boeing XB-47 and Northrop F-89) suppressing Dutch roll and gun-platform oscillation.
Hughes E-1 (AN/APG-33) and Westinghouse AN/APS-21 automatic radar target tracking and lead-pursuit steering display (F-94A/B, F-89B/C, F3D-2).
Flight Refuelling probe-and-drogue and Boeing flying-boom receptacles (tested operationally on F-80C and F-84G).
Hughes E-4/E-5/E-9 (AN/APG-37 and AN/APG-40) analog fire-control computers steering interceptors onto a single-pass collision course to automatically ripple-fire FFAR rockets (F-86D, F-94C, F-89D).
Mil-spec subminiature vacuum tubes, potted modules, and etched printed-circuit boards reducing avionics weight and vibration failures.
Hughes MG-10/MG-13 AWCS (F-102A, F-101B) and Westinghouse AN/APQ-50 (F4D-1, F3H-2) coupling CW illuminators and autopilot steering for Falcon and Sparrow missiles.
MIT Lincoln Lab / USAF AN/FSQ-7 SAGE ground-to-air Time Division Data Link (AN/ARR-60/61), vectoring ADC interceptors hands-off to target intercept.
Silicon junction transistors and magnetic-core airborne digital memory replacing high-failure vacuum-tube racks.
Passive lead-sulfide infrared search and track (IRST) sensors (F-101B, F-102A, F-106A, F4H-1, F8U-2N) for ECM-resistant target tracking.
Hughes MA-1 Digitair (F-106A) and Westinghouse AN/APQ-72 (F4H-1 Phantom II) long-range high-power radars and integrated weapon systems.
WWII standard Browning AN/M2 .50-cal machine guns, US Navy Hispano AN/M3 20mm cannon, 5-inch HVAR rockets, and 6-pylon wing racks.
Browning AN/M3 .50-caliber machine gun firing 1,200 rpm for brief jet firing windows (F-84, F-86A/E/F).
NOTS 2.75-inch Mk 4 Mighty Mouse folding-fin aerial rocket and electrically primed M24 20mm cannon for anti-bomber interception.
Pontiac T-160 / M39 20mm revolver cannon (tested in Korea on F-86F-2 GunVal; standard on F-100/F-101) and Colt Mk 12 20mm Navy cannon.
Low-Altitude Bombing System (LABS) gyro-timed over-the-shoulder toss-bombing computer and Mk 7 tactical nuclear store wiring (F-84G, F-100D, F-105).
High-speed snap-action internal weapons bay doors and trapeze launchers eliminating external store wave drag on supersonic interceptors (F-102A, F-101B, F-105, F-106A).
Project Hotshot / Sperry AAM-N-2 (AIM-7A) Sparrow I radar beam-riding air-to-air missile.
Hughes MX-904 / GAR-1 (AIM-4A) Falcon first-generation semi-active radar homing interceptor missile.
Bill McLean's China Lake AIM-9B Sidewinder and Hughes GAR-2A (AIM-4C) uncooled lead-sulfide (PbS) rear-aspect IR homing missiles.
General Electric Project Vulcan T-171 / M61 20mm 6-barrel Gatling gun (6,000 rpm) for F-104 and F-105.
Douglas MB-1 / AIR-2A Genie unguided nuclear rocket (1.5 kt W25 warhead, live-tested in Operation Plumbbob Shot John 1957).
Raytheon AIM-7C Sparrow III CW semi-active radar homing BVR missile (F3H-2M, F4H-1) and Hughes GAR-11 (AIM-26A) Nuclear Falcon.
T.P. Wright's 80% aircraft learning curve, master plaster lofting, and WWII moving assembly line practices.
NACA coin-dimpled flush riveting and milled butt-joint skin tolerances reducing turbulent skin-friction drag on jet fighters.
Optical alignment telescopes and collimator reference lines replacing heavy steel master gauges for swept-wing assembly jigs.
USAF Heavy Press Program (35,000 and 50,000-ton Wyman-Gordon/Alcoa closed-die forging presses) producing single-piece wing bulkheads and spars.
MIL-Q-5923 ultrasonic/X-ray non-destructive inspection and statistical process control on Korean War surge production lines.
North American Aviation 'Chem-Mill' chemical etching of curved skins and heated-die inert-gas titanium forming/welding.
MIT Servomechanisms Lab / USAF APT punched-tape 3-axis numerically controlled (NC) skin and spar mills.
NACA high-speed subsonic tunnels (choked at M0.85-1.18) and small intermittent supersonic nozzle tunnels above M1.2.
NACA Wallops Island Pilotless Aircraft Research Division (PARD) rocket-boosted free-flight models and wing-flow transonic bumps bridging the transonic gap before slotted tunnels.
NACA Muroc multi-channel strain-gauge oscillographs and FM/FM real-time radio telemetry from X-1/D-558 test flights.
Ray Wright & Richard Whitcomb's NACA Langley 8-Foot and 16-Foot slotted-throat transonic wind tunnels (Collier Trophy 1951), eliminating transonic choking.
Dynamic aeroelastic wind-tunnel models, ground vibration shake tests, and Reeves REAC analog computers solving coupled bending-torsion flutter equations.
IBM 701 'Defense Calculator' (delivered to Lockheed, North American, Douglas, Convair, Boeing, GE in 1953) and IBM 704 FORTRAN (1956) revolutionizing aero/structural matrix calculations.
NACA/Edwards 5-DOF & 6-DOF real-time analog-digital flight simulators following the 1954 X-3 and F-100A roll-inertia coupling accidents (validating Phillips' 1948 NACA TN-1627).
USAF/NACA Stability and Control Handbook (early DATCOM), AEDC Tullahoma Propulsion Wind Tunnel, and automated magnetic-tape flight-test data reduction.
